195771773_2251c6d3.text: In addition to LP, the lateral dorsal nucleus of the thalamus (LD) is yet another "higher order" thalamic nucleus that has connections to various pathways including visual, limbic, and somatosensory (Bezdudnaya et al., 2008)Jones, 1985;(Robertson et al., 1981) (Takahashi, 1985). In the rat, the ventral lateral part of this nucleus (LDVL) receives input from both primary and secondary visual cortex, while the medial portion does not (Takahashi, 1985). Beyond this tracing study, there is remarkably little research on involvement of this relatively large nucleus in visual circuits. We find that like LP, LD also projects to all visual cortical areas in the mouse.
195771773_2251c6d3.section: Location, anatomical identity, and functional context of LD
